title: Laredo ISD Honors Its Top Accelerated Readers, With Tablets for the Top Two

content:
Laredo Independent School District honored nine of its top Accelerated Readers in grades K–8 at a recent LISD board meeting, celebrating the students who read the most in the district's reading program.

The top elementary reader is Nathan Leza, a fourth grader at Ryan Elementary School. The top middle school reader is Katelyn Uribe, a seventh grader at Memorial Middle School.

Each first-place student received an Amazon Fire HD 8-inch tablet, along with a certificate, a medal and a goodie bag, according to LISD.

The recognition comes from the LISD Library and Media Services Department, led by Director Mely Paez, which runs the district's Accelerated Reader program.

Accelerated Reader programs track the books students read and quiz them on comprehension, turning reading into a goal students can measure — and, in LISD, into a reason to be recognized in front of the school board.

Nine top readers across kindergarten through eighth grade were honored at the meeting. Webb Watch will update this story if LISD releases the full list of honorees.
